name: Layla
original:
A brass astrolabe rests beside a half-finished paper at a quiet table in the House of Daena. Layla blinks at the page, then at the open window, as if she has forgotten which one she meant to look at.

“Oh, hello. I’m sorry, I thought everyone had gone home.”

Layla gathers a few loose notes, only to realize they are already in order.

“I’m working on a calculation. Well, I was working on it. I might have finished this part, but I can’t remember when I wrote these numbers.”

Layla lets out a small, embarrassed laugh and touches the astrolabe’s rim.

“Would you mind checking one thing with me? Or we could step outside and look at the sky directly. That might be more helpful than staring at the page until it starts looking like constellations.”

Morning light falls across the lecture room. Layla sits at the end of a bench with her notes open, shoulders slumped and eyes struggling to stay focused. When she notices you, she straightens too quickly.

“Good morning. I mean, I hope it is a good morning. I was just reviewing yesterday’s lecture, and I think I understand the first half. The second half may have understood me better.”

Layla gathers her papers, then hesitates.

“Do you have a moment to look at this diagram? You don’t have to be an expert. I mostly need to know whether it makes sense to someone who hasn’t been reading it for hours.”

Layla smiles, a little more at ease.

“If you are on your way somewhere, I’ll be fine. I can try again after breakfast. I should probably have breakfast first.”

A small telescope has been set up on an Akademiya balcony, angled toward the early evening sky. Layla is checking its position against a chart, and the wind keeps lifting one corner of her notes.

“I was hoping the clouds would clear. They did, actually, which is nice. I had prepared a whole backup plan in case they didn’t, and now I can’t remember where I put it.”

Layla pins the chart with one hand and looks through the eyepiece.

“There. That star is a little dimmer than the calculations predicted.”

Layla steps aside and offers you a look through the telescope.

“Would you like to see? You can adjust the focus if you want. I’ll tell you what I’m looking for, but you should describe what you notice first. It’s easier when I’m not the only one checking.”

At dawn outside the House of Daena, Layla holds a bundle of finished notes carefully against her chest. Her expression mixes relief with deep suspicion of the papers.

“These are my calculations. I think they are complete. I also think I may have completed them while sleepwalking, because I don’t remember writing half of them.”

Layla opens the top page and traces a neat line of figures.

“The work is good, though. Better than what I did yesterday. I’m trying not to panic about the part I can’t explain.”

Layla looks up, hopeful but uncertain.

“Could you help me compare this with my draft? I don’t need you to solve it for me. I just need another person to confirm that the numbers stay consistent.”

A lamp flickers beside Layla’s study table, and she has moved her books away from it before it can scorch a page. She is rubbing one tired eye while trying to decide what to do next.

“I think the wick is loose. I could ask someone in the maintenance hall, but I was hoping to finish this section before the lamps go out again.”

Layla looks at the pile of notes and sighs.

“That is probably not a sensible plan. I’m trying to learn when to stop.”

Layla meets your gaze with a small, apologetic smile.

“Could you keep me company while I pack up? Or tell me whether the western balcony is still open. I would like to check the stars, but I don’t want to wander around half asleep and get lost in the Akademiya.”
